input_text: Sentence: SOCCER - JAPAN GET LUCKY WIN, CHINA IN SURPRISE DEFEAT. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Nadim Ladki Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: AL-AIN, United Arab Emirates 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Japan began the defence of their Asian Cup title with a lucky 2-1 win against Syria in a Group C championship match on Friday. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: But China saw their luck desert them in the second match of the group, crashing to a surprise 2-0 defeat to newcomers Uzbekistan. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: China controlled most of the match and saw several chances missed until the 78th minute when Uzbek striker Igor Shkvyrin took advantage of a misdirected defensive header to lob the ball over the advancing Chinese keeper and into an empty net. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Oleg Shatskiku made sure of the win in injury time, hitting an unstoppable left foot shot from just outside the area. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The former Soviet republic was playing in an Asian Cup finals tie for the first time. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Despite winning the Asian Games title two years ago, Uzbekistan are in the finals as outsiders. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Two goals from defensive errors in the last six minutes allowed Japan to come from behind and collect all three points from their opening meeting against Syria. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Takuya Takagi scored the winner in the 88th minute, rising to head a Hiroshige Yanagimoto cross towards the Syrian goal which goalkeeper Salem Bitar appeared to have covered but then allowed to slip into the net. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: It was the second costly blunder by Syria in four minutes. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Defender Hassan Abbas rose to intercept a long ball into the area in the 84th minute but only managed to divert it into the top corner of Bitar's goal. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Nader Jokhadar had given Syria the lead with a well-struck header in the seventh minute. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Japan then laid siege to the Syrian penalty area for most of the game but rarely breached the Syrian defence. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Bitar pulled off fine saves whenever they did. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Japan coach Shu Kamo said:'' The Syrian own goal proved lucky for us. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The Syrians scored early and then played defensively and adopted long balls which made it hard for us.' Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: ' Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Japan, co-hosts of the World Cup in 2002 and ranked 20th in the world by FIFA, are favourites to regain their title here. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Hosts UAE play Kuwait and South Korea take on Indonesia on Saturday in Group A matches. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: All four teams are level with one point each from one game. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: ROME 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Italy recalled Marcello Cuttitta Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: on Friday for their friendly against Scotland at Murrayfield more than a year after the 30-year-old wing announced he was retiring following differences over selection. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Cuttitta, who trainer George Coste said was certain to play on Saturday week, was named in a 21-man squad lacking only two of the team beaten 54-21 by England at Twickenham last month. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Stefano Bordon is out through illness and Coste said he had dropped back row Corrado Covi, who had been recalled for the England game after five years out of the national team. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Cuttitta announced his retirement after the 1995 World Cup, where he took issue with being dropped from the Italy side that faced England in the pool stages. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Coste said he had approached the player two months ago about a comeback. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "He ended the World Cup on the wrong note," Coste said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "I thought it would be useful to have him back and he said he would be available. Following the order: first to last Entity:

input_text: Sentence: SOCCER - LATE GOALS GIVE JAPAN WIN OVER SYRIA. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: AL-AIN, United Arab Emirates 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Two goals in the last six minutes gave holders Japan an uninspiring 2-1 Asian Cup victory over Syria on Friday. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Takuya Takagi headed the winner in the 88th minute of the group C game after goalkeeper Salem Bitar spoiled a mistake-free display by allowing the ball to slip under his body. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: It was the second Syrian defensive blunder in four minutes. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Defender Hassan Abbas rose to intercept a long ball into the area in the 84th minute but only managed to divert it into the top corner of Bitar's goal. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Syria had taken the lead from their first serious attack in the seventh minute. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Nader Jokhadar headed a cross from the right by Ammar Awad into the top right corner of Kenichi Shimokawa's goal. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Japan then laid siege to the Syrian penalty area and had a goal disallowed for offside in the 16th minute. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: A minute later, Bitar produced a good double save, first from Kazuyoshi Miura's header and then blocked a Takagi follow-up shot. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Bitar saved well again from Miura in the 37th minute, parrying away his header from a corner. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Japan started the second half brightly but Bitar denied them an equaliser when he dived to his right to save Naoki Soma's low drive in the 53rd minute. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Robert Kitson Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: LONDON 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Centre Jason Little will miss Australia's end-of-tour fixture against the Barbarians at Twickenham on Saturday. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Little has opted not to risk aggravating the knee injury which ruled him out of a large chunk of the tour and is replaced by fellow Queenslander Daniel Herbert. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Owen Finegan has recovered from the knocks he took in last weekend's test against Wales and retains his place in the back-row ahead of Daniel Manu. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The Wallabies have their sights set on a 13th successive victory to end their European tour with a 100 percent record but also want to turn on the style and provide David Campese with a fitting send-off in his final match in Australian colours. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The Wallabies currently have no plans to make any special presentation to the 34-year-old winger but a full house of 75,000 spectators will still gather in the hope of witnessing one last moment of magic. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Campese will be up against a familiar foe in the shape of Barbarians captain Rob Andrew, the man who kicked Australia to defeat with a last-ditch drop-goal in the World Cup quarter-final in Cape Town. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "Campo has a massive following in this country and has had the public with him ever since he first played here in 1984," said Andrew, also likely to be making his final Twickenham appearance. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: On tour, Australia have won all four tests against Italy, Scotland, Ireland and Wales, and scored 414 points at an average of almost 35 points a game. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Australia gave Brian Lara another reason to be miserable when they beat West Indies by five wickets in the opening World Series limited overs match on Friday. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Lara, disciplined for misconduct on Wednesday, was dismissed for five to extend a disappointing run of form on tour. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Australia, who hold a 2-0 lead in the five-match test series, overhauled West Indies' total of 172 all out with eight balls to spare to end a run of six successive one-day defeats. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: All-rounder Greg Blewett steered his side to a comfortable victory with an unbeaten 57 in 90 balls to the delight of the 42,442 crowd. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Man-of-the match Blewett came to the wicket with the total on 70 for two and hit three fours during an untroubled innings lasting 129 minutes. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: His crucial fifth-wicket partnership with fellow all-rounder Stuart Law, who scored 21, added 71 off 85 balls. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Lara looked out of touch during his brief stay at the crease before chipping a simple catch to Shane Warne at mid-wicket. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: West Indies tour manager Clive Lloyd has apologised for Lara's behaviour on Tuesday. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: He (Lara) had told Australia coach Geoff Marsh that wicketkeeper Ian Healy was unwelcome in the visitors' dressing room. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The Melbourne crowd were clearly angered by the incident, loudly jeering the West Indies vice-captain as he walked to the middle. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: It was left to fellow left-hander Shivnarine Chanderpaul to hold the innings together with a gritty 54 despite the handicap of an injured groin. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Chanderpaul was forced to rely on a runner for most of his innings after hurting himself as he scurried back to his crease to avoid being run out. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Pakistan, who arrive in Australia later this month, are the other team competing in the World Series tournament. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: West Indies batsman Brian Lara suffered another blow to his Australian tour, after already being disciplined for misconduct, when he was dismissed cheaply in the first limited overs match against Australia on Friday. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Lara, who earned a stern rebuke from his own tour management after an angry outburst against Australia wicketkeeper Ian Healy, scored five to prolong a run of poor form with the bat. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The West Indies vice-captain struggled for timing during his 36-minute stay at the crease before chipping a ball from medium pacer Tom Moody straight to Shane Warne at mid-wicket. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: West Indies were 53 for two in 15 overs when rain stopped play at the Melbourne Cricket Ground after captain Courtney Walsh won the toss and elected to bat. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Lara's outburst three days ago has clearly turned some of the Australian public against him. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: As he walked to the wicket he was greeted by loud jeers from sections of the crowd. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: On several occasions during his innings, the crowd joined together in a series of obscene chants against him. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Tour manager Clive Lloyd on Wednesday apologised for Lara's behaviour in confronting Australia coach Geoff Marsh in the opposition dressing room to protest against his dismissal in the second test on Tuesday. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Lloyd did not say what form the discipline would take. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Lara, who holds the record for the highest score in test and first-class cricket, was unhappy about Healy's role in the incident and questioned whether the ball had carried to the Australia keeper. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Australia went on to win the match at the Sydney Cricket Ground by 124 runs to take a two-nil lead in the five-test series after Lara failed in both innings. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Lara has yet to score a century since West Indies arrived in Australia five weeks ago. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Both West Indies and Australia team management have played down the incident, stressing that relations between the two sides have not been adversely affected. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Ohio State left tackle Orlando Pace became the first repeat winner of the Lombardi Award Thursday night when the Rotary Club of Houston again honoured him as college football's lineman of the year. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: At least four people have been shot dead in two suspected political attacks in South Africa's volatile Zulu heartland, police said on Friday. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The victims were 18 and 20, he said, adding one other youth had been wounded in the shooting. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: In another attack, also on the province's south coast on Thursday night, two men were shot dead near Umkomaas. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "We suspect that these killings are linked to politics," spokesman Bala Naidoo told Reuters. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: There had been no arrests. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The killings came just hours after violence monitors said they were not optimistic of a peaceful festive season in KwaZulu-Natal and pointed the south coast region where 18 people were massacred last Christmas as one of potential hot spots. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Klara Gajduskova Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Czech President Vaclav Havel on Friday welcomed the appointment of Madeleine Albright, who is of Czech extraction, as the United States' first woman Secretary of State. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: In a statement Havel, who is recovering from cancer surgery, said: "Madeleine Albright is a distinguished friend, a tested diplomat, and a true American of fine origins." Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "I look forward to continuing our good relations ... Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: with the United States and with the first woman ever to hold the position of Secretary of State. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: I wish her well, "Havel said in a statement to Reuters. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Havel, who helped lead the "velvet revolution" that ousted the Communist regime in Prague in 1989, invited Albright, then working for a private foreign policy think tank, to advise his new democratic government in 1990. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Havel had a small malignant tumour removed from his lung on Monday and is recovering in hospital. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Albright, born Marie Korbelova to a Czechoslovak diplomat in 1937, fled with her family to the United States after the Communists came to power in a coup in 1948. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: As an academic, Albright studied and lectured on Europe's 20th century problems before becoming U.S. ambassador to the United Nations. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Czech diplomats, seeking to have their country included in the expected expansion of NATO, praised the selection of Albright, known to be a strong supporter of alliance's integration of former Soveit-bloc countries. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "The nomination ... Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: is a clear signal that one key of the lines of foreign policy will be the strengthening of the trans-Atlantic cooperation, a creation of strategic partnership between Europe and the US, "Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec told Reuters. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "(Albright) is a convinced advocate of NATO enlargement and of stabilisation of security structures." Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Czech ambassador to the United Nations, Karel Kovanda, told the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes that Albright "is a little light in our diplomatic heaven," but warned against expecting her to exert any influence in favour of the Czechs. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: POLAND GOT MONEY FROM POST-WAR SWISS ACCOUNTS. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Marcin Grajewski Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: WARSAW 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Poland said on Friday that Swiss bank accounts, which in many cases belonged to Polish Jews who died in the Holocaust, were used in debt settlements between the two countries after the World War Two. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati, unveiling first findings of a special government commission, said that in 1970s the then communist Poland received 460,000 Swiss francs from the accounts. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "In 1970s, Poland received from unclaimed accounts in Switzerland a sum of 460,000 francs. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: What was its right (to the money) ...I do not know, "Rosati told a news conference. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Switzerland stands accused by Senator Alfonse D'Amato, chairman of the powerful U.S. Senate Banking Committee, of agreeing to give money to Poland from unclaimed bank accounts of Polish citizens, as part of an accord on compensating Swiss nationals whose assets had been seized in communist Poland. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Many of these citizens were Jews murdered during the war, when Nazi German invaders killed most of Poland's 3.5 million Jews. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Rosati did not say whether the payment in 1970s was part of the 1949 agreement between Warsaw and Switzerland on compensation to Swiss citizens whose assets were seized by the Soviet-imposed communists authorities after World War Two. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "I expect that the commission will finish gathering information within two to three weeks and then more details will be provided," Rosati said. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Rosati confirmed that the 1949 agreement had provided for granting Switzerland about 53 million francs and most of this sum was repaid with coal exports. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: He said, however, that Switzerland did get about 16,000 francs from the so-called "dead accounts" as part of the compensation. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "About 16,000 francs were seized from accounts of four or five Polish citizens, whose data we do not precisely know. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The issue is of moral and legal nature, because its financial significance is small, "Rosati said. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Under pressure from international Jewish organisations, Swiss government has devised a plan to pay out millions of dollars in unclaimed bank accounts as a conciliatory gesture toward Holocaust victims. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The conservative Radical Democrats (FDP) have said they would ask parliament next week to order Swiss banks to put some 40 million Swiss francs ($31 million) in dormant wealth into a fund earmarked for Jewish groups and charitable organisations. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: But Swiss banks and the country's Jewish community voiced doubts whether the plan would work. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: They said the Santa Fe deal, which includes desirable Nevada mining territory, would only payoff for Newmont longer term. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Newmont, in fact, will not benefit from the Santa Fe acquisition on an earnings basis for at least two years, which also limits its capacity to raise its offer. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Any deal, friendly or hostile, would almost assuredly be a stock swap, which is necessary to preserve the tax-free, pooling-of-interest accounting, they said. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: A Homestake spokesman was not immediately available to comment on speculation that it tops the list. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Chile and Mexico will start negotiations next year to broaden their free trade agreement to include services and investments, Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat said. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Chile hopes to broaden the treaty signed in 1994 beyond reduction of tariffs on imports and exports and add provisions covering services and investment codes, said Aninat. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: '' In January or February, we'll have some very close contacts with Mexico to add the issue of services and advance on the issue of investments,'' Aninat told reporters after signing a free trade deal with Canada. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Aninat also said he was confident the Chilean Congress would ratify the treaty with Congress quickly. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Indonesia's Belo leaves for Nobel award ceremony. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: DILI, East Timor 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: East Timorese Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo left Dili on Friday on his way to Norway for the awards ceremony as co-recipient of the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Witnesses said Belo left the territory for the Indonesian capital Jakarta accompanied by five other people. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: It was not immediately known when he would arrive in Oslo. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The bishop will jointly receive the Nobel award next Tuesday with East Timorese-born activist Jose Ramos Horta, who lives in self-exile in Australia. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The Indonesian government has condemned the inclusion of Ramos Horta in the award, and Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Friday that Indonesia would not be represented officially at the ceremony in the Norwegian capital. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "I sincerely believe that this unfortunate choice in giving the honour to such a controversial figure as Ramos Horta ... Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: will exacerbate the problem in finding a solution (to East Timor), "Alatas said on Friday. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: He was responding to questions at a news conference called to discuss next week's ministerial meeting of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) in Jakarta. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Ramos Horta has been a vocal leader of the opposition to Jakarta's rule in the territory. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Belo and Ramos Horta were awared the prize for their efforts to secure a peaceful solution to the issue of East Timor, a former Portuguese colony which Indonesia invaded in 1975 and annexed the following year. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The United Nations has never recognised Jakarta's move. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Alatas said the government's position on the Nobel Peace Prize would have been different if it had been awarded solely to Belo. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Asked if the Indonesian ambassador to Norway would have attended the ceremony if only Belo had been involved, Alatas replied: "Probably, yes, but that is a hypothetical question." Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Alatas said on Tuesday that on his way back from Oslo, Belo would visit the Vatican to see the Pope, and would also meet German Chancellor Helmut Kohl in Bonn. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Kohl had wanted to meet Belo during the chancellor's official visit to Indonesia last month, but the bishop was too busy in East Timor to come to Jakarta. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Government disperses protest with water cannons. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: RANGOON 1996-12-07 Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Burmese troops and riot police moved in to disperse a student street protest at a suburban road junction near the Ranyon (Rangoon) University early on Saturday, witnesses said. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: They said police and troops used water cannons from fire engines to subdue about 120 university students sitting in at the centre of the junction at about 3 a.m. before they moved in to round them up. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The students, who had staged an 11-hour protest at the junction in northern Rangoon, were taken away in three vehicles. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The witnesses said some of the students were hit with batons while they were herded onto the vehicles and it was believed they were taken to the Insein prison in suburban Rangoon. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The protesting students, mostly from Rangoon University, were demanding the right to organise independent unions on campuses and the release of about 80 student leaders currently in jail. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: They were among 500 students who started demonstrating at the intersection on late Friday afternoon. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The protest was the second major one in five days in the capital. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Burmese students march briefly out of campus. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Vithoon Amorn Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: RANGOON 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: About 200 Burmese students marched briefly from troubled Yangon Institute of Technology in northern Rangoon on Friday towards the University of Yangon six km (four miles) away, and returned to their campus, witnesses said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Seven truckloads of armed riot police and three fire engines were on standby at one of the junctions near the institute. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: There were no clashes. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "They are now back in the YIT campus," an institute official who declined to be identified told Reuters by telephone. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: One of two roads leading to the University of Yangon from the institute had been closed by authorities. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: But about 300 university students were still gathered outside the gates of their campus, witnesses said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: They were singing peacefully. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: On Monday and Tuesday, students from the institute and the university launched protests against what they said was unfair handling by police of a brawl between some of their colleagues and restaurant owners in October. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: On Tuesday and Wednesday, opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi was restricted to her home by the military government to prevent her from being drawn into the protests. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: She was allowed to move freely on Thursday. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The protest culminated at dawn on Tuesday with several hundred students being detained briefly by police in central Rangoon. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The street protests were the biggest seen in the capital since the student-led pro-democracry demonstrations of September 1988 when the junta crushed the uprising. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Thousands were killed or imprisoned. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Earlier on Friday some of the students, who were held briefly by police during the protests earlier this week, said they were still dissatisfied with the military government. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: They told Reuters they were unhappy that the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) had not heeded their calls for the right to organise independent unions on campus. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "We still want government answers to our demands. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: We want police punishment to be published in newspapers, "one student said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: But the students stressed their protests were non-political and they had no contact with Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD). Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Suu Kyi, a Nobel laureate and daughter of independence hero Aung San, and key NLD officials have also denied any link with the students. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: But they have said both parties had a "moral link" in that they were against police brutality and injustice. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The students also demanded the government announce punishments meted out to policemen who they said had manhandled students involved in a brawl with some restaurant owners near the Yangon institute in October. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The students appealed to the government not to close the institute because of their latest demonstration. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The institute was shut for nearly two years after the 1988 uprising. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: On Friday, the road leading to Suu Kyi's lakeside residence in central Rangoon remained closed by police. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Bill Jordan, general secretary of the International Confederation of Free Trade Unions (ICFTU), told a news conference the withdrawal of a WTO invitation to ILO director general Michel Hansenne was "outrageous behaviour on the part of an organisation that wants to command respect in the world". Sentence: Indian rubber demand seen outstripping production. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: SINGAPORE 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Indian rubber demand is seen outpacing local production in the 1996/97 April / March season and the trend will persist way into the next century, the chairman of the Rubber Board of India said on Friday. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: K.J. Matthew said at the Asia Rubber Markets meeting here Indian production of natural rubber in 1996/97 will reach 547,000 tonnes against projected demand of 578,000 tonnes, a gap of 31,000 tonnes. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: For synthetic rubber, production reached 68,200 tonnes in 1995/96 while consumption in the same season hit 134,085 tonnes, Matthew added. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "Though schemes designed to realise further increases in the production of natural rubber are being operated successfully, the demand-supply gap is expected to widen," he said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Indian synthetic rubber output is not expected to rise significantly in the next season but demand will rise to 145,000 tonnes. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Matthew estimates that by the 2000/01 season, the gap between natural rubber output and consumption will rise to 51,000 tonnes and 319,000 tonnes in 2010/11. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Natural rubber production will go up to 695,000 tonnes in 2000/01 against consumption of 746,000 tonnes. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: In 2010/11, domestic demand should rise further to 1.233 million tonnes while production will only reach about 914,000 tonnes. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: One way to bridge the widening gap is to put more land under cultivation which the Rubber Board official estimates will reach 220,000 hectares between now and the year 2003 although Matthew said this may not be possible at this time in India. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "The development objective for the rubber plantation industry will be to increase production to the best extent possibly with a view to minimising imports of natural rubber," he said. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Japan's authorities seen seeking to rein in dollar. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: George Nishiyama Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: TOKYO 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Comments by Japan's tight-lipped central bank chief and an influential top bureaucrat are further signs that the nation's authorities want to keep the dollar at current levels, market sources said on Friday. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: In a rare expression of a view on currencies by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor, Yasuo Matsushita was quoted in Japan's leading economic daily on Friday as saying that he sees no further, immediate fall in the yen. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: This followed a widely watched television appearance late on Thursday by Eisuke Sakakibara, a high-ranking Finance Ministry official, who denied he had said he wants to guide the dollar lower to between 108 and 110 yen. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: But many in the market thought Sakakibara's real intentions lay elsewhere, and took more notice of his comments about the U.S. government's stance on the dollar, dealers said. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "I think his views on (U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert) Rubin's comments were indeed what he himself thinks about the dollar," said Hank Note, chief dealer at Sumitomo Bank. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Asked about Rubin's comment that a strong dollar was in U.S. interests, Sakakibara said the remark does not necessarily mean the United States supports a stronger dollar. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "It's a strong dollar, not stronger. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: In that sense, the comments are not pointing to a certain direction, "he said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "It shows that Sakakibara is not for a stronger dollar either," said Sumitomo's Note. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Takao Sakoh, first vice president at Union Bank of Switzerland in Tokyo, said: "Maybe a dollar at 104.50 yen is not acceptable (to Sakakibara), but it may be okay at the current level, at the lower end of 112 yen." Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Market participants have kept a close eye on Sakakibara, chief of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, as a comment he made in November after the dollar hit this year's high of 114.92 yen pushed the currency down sharply. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: He had said then that the market's view on Japan's economy was too pessimistic and that he believed it was stronger than the market thought. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Dealers have come to refer to 115 yen as the "Sakakibara ceiling" for the dollar following the remark. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Adding to the comments by "Mr Yen", as Sakakibara is known for his prominence in the currency market, was BOJ governor Matsushita's remark. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "The recent level of the yen exchange rate has been stable, and it does not appear to be moving towards a further depreciation of the yen immediately, so import prices are likely to stabilise at current levels," Matsushita said in an interview with the Nihon Keizai Shimbun. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "The fact that he touched on the issue of inflation triggered by import prices shows that the BOJ does not want a further depreciation of the yen, past 115 yen," said Yasuhito Kawashima, chief forex manager at Toyo Trust & Banking Co. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Some said the central bank may have been concerned a weaker yen would lead to unfounded pessimism about Japan's economy. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "There was concern that foreign investors may sell Japanese stocks if the dollar goes above 115 yen. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The BOJ does not want the yen's weakness to lead to pessimism over the economy, "said Taisuke Tanaka, market strategist with Credit Suisse in Tokyo. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Senior BOJ officials have separately said financial markets' views on the economy have been too negative. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "I realise there are negative views in the markets about the impact of the consumption tax hike and drop in public spending, but the markets appear to be exaggerating the magnitude of the negative impact," a senior BOJ official told Reuters on Friday. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The consumption tax is due to raised in April from three to five percent. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Lebanon sentences pro-Israeli warlord to death. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Haitham Haddadin Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: BEIRUT 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: A Lebanese military court on Friday sentenced to death in absentia the commander of Israel's surrogate militia in south Lebanon on treason charges. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The court convicted General Antoine Lahd, head of the South Lebanon Army (SLA), of collaborating with Israel with which Lebanon is officially at war. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Lahd, a 69-year-old former Lebanese army major-general, heads the 3,000-strong SLA militia which helps Israel hold a border zone in south Lebanon to ward off cross-frontier guerrilla raids on northern Israel. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Lahd said a few days after the trial began on February 16 that Lebanese authorities must drop the charges or risk blocking any peace deal with the Jewish state. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: He said Israel was capable of pressuring Lebanon's Syrian-backed government to stop the legal pursuit. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The charges against Lahd were: forming a hostile army, carrying weapons on Israel's side, helping Israel strip off a part of Lebanese territory by violence, forming an armed gang, killing or trying to kill Lebanese civilians by artillery shelling and kidnapping Lebanese citizens for long periods. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Shortly before Lahd's trial began, a Beirut military prosecutor charged another 89 former Lebanese army soldiers with collaborating with Israel. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: No date has been set for the trial of the men, all members of the SLA living in the Israeli-held zone in south Lebanon. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Israel and Lahd have repeatedly demanded safety guarantees for the SLA -- a mixed Christian-Shi'ite Moslem force -- which the Jewish states regards as loyal allies. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Israel has said the Lebanese army must incorporate the SLA fighters into its ranks as an army brigade as a condition for peace. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: But Lebanese political analysts have said that would be out of the question and Lebanese authorities pre-empted the issue by taking legal action against Lahd. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Former Israeli Prime Minister Shimon Peres, calling Lahd "a great Lebanese patriot", said earlier this year Lebanon had insulted the SLA commander by ordering his arrest on the treason charges. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Peres, who was ousted in May by rightwing Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu, said there could not be real negotiations with Lebanon "unless it will stop the maltreatment of the SLA and its commanders." Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The Beirut military court also sentenced to life in jail in absentia Etian Saqr, former head of the pro-Israeli Guardians of the Cedars, a small rightwing Christian civil war militia. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Saqr, whose trial was concurrent with Lahd's, was convicted of "contacting the Israeli enemy, passing information to Israel and undertaking hostile acts against Lebanon". Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: 14 years later, Florida man dies for killing. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: TALLAHASSEE, Fla. 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Fourteen years after he bludgeoned and shot a man whose trailer home he robbed in 1982, John Mills Jr. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: , 41, was put to death in Florida's electric chair Friday. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: As Glenn Lawhon, a rural Florida minister who is the victim's father, looked on, Mills was pronounced dead at 7:13 a.m. EST (1213 GMT) for the murder of Lester Lawhon. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Speaking in Arabic, Mills made a final statement before an anonymous citizen flipped the switch that sent 2000 volts of electricity through his body, said Department of Corrections spokesman Eugene Morris, who was present at the execution. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "I bear witness that there is no God but Allah and I bear witness that the prophet Mohammed is the messenger of God," he quoted Mills as saying. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Prison officials said they had no record of Mills' official conversion, but they said that, on May 14, 1991, he had asked that a new name, Yuhanna Abdullah Muhammed, be added to his prison file, which is usually an indication of a conversion to Islam. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Mills is the 38th person to die in Florida's electric chair since the U.S. Supreme Court reversed itself in 1976 and legalised the death penalty. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Prison officials said Mills made no special request for a last meal and did not eat the steak, fried potatoes and orange juice offered him. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: He spent Thursday with family members and his spiritual adviser, Morris said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Mills was scheduled to die Wednesday but had his sentence temporarily postponed by the Florida Supreme Court. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: On Thursday, the 11th Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals in Atlanta denied his appeal in federal court. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: In March 1982, Mills and accomplice Michael Frederick knocked on the door of Lester Lawhon's trailer in an attempt to rob it, police said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Lester Lawhon was taken to a nearby airstrip where he was bludgeoned with a tire iron. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Mills then fired two shots that killed Lawhon as the victim tried to run away. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Frederick is serving a 347-year sentence. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Half of dog bites provoked, says American vet. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: CHICAGO 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: As many as 1 million dog bites are recorded in the United States every year and half of them are provoked by humans, a veterinarian told fellow animal doctors on Friday. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The Humane Society of the United States estimates that between 500,000 and one million bites are delivered by dogs each year, more than half of which are suffered by children. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "Most bites can be prevented by teaching children how to respect a dog," Michael Cornwell of the Glencoe Animal Hospital in Columbus, Ohio, told the annual meeting of the American Veterinary Medical Association. Following the order: first to last Entity:

input_text: Sentence: "Let's not let our kids jump on them or crawl on them. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Dogs and children don't have to have an interaction. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Cornwell said 50 percent of reported bites were provoked by a person and 60 percent were suffered by children. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: He also estimated that only 25 percent of bites were reported because medical attention was not needed. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Don Rieck, president of the National Animal Control Association, said aggressiveness in dogs was related more to gender than breed and a male dog that had not been neutered was three times more likely to bite than an unspayed female. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The five breeds credited with the most incidents were chow chows, Rottweilers, German shepherds, cocker spaniels and Dalmatians. " Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The trends in dog bites by particular breeds have more to do with fad pets owned by individuals who need to have something unique. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Speaking strictly of dogs, 15 years ago the macho fad pet was a Doberman. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Today, Rottweilers are on the way up, "Rieck said. Following the order: first to last Entity:

input_text: Sentence: Representatives of the U.N. missions of Ghana, the Ivory Coast, Mauritania and Niger have scheduled a meeting with Security Council president Paolo Fulci of Italy to hand in the nominations in writing, the envoys said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: It was not known if other candidates would step forward. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Diplomats said General Joseph Garba of Nigeria, a U.N. General Assembly president in 1989-90, was putting forth his own candidacy without being nominated by his country. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Boutros-Ghali on Wednesday opened the door for other Africans to contest his job by saying he was suspending temporarily his candidacy but was not withdrawing completely from the race. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: His supporters said this meant he remained a candidate in case the race reached an impasse. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The United States on Nov. 19 vetoed his bid for re-election while the other 14 Security Council members supported him. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The move by the African states means that the council could begin voting on candidates next week, a procedure that could either result in a decision or turn into a bitter fight with vetoes against each nominee. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: EU, Poland agree on oil import tariffs. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: BRUSSELS 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The European Union and Poland have resolved disagreements over a new Polish oil import regime, the European Commission said on Friday. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The EU had objected to increases in Polish tariffs on imports of gasoline and gasoil products introduced on January 1, 1996, saying they contravened levels envisaged in the so-called Europe Agreement between the EU and Poland. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The increases were aimed at protecting the Polish market while helping to modernise the local oil industry. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "The EU and Poland have now reached a final settlement regarding issues related to the Polish import regime in the oils sector," the Commission said in a statement. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Under the agreement, Poland will abolish all oil import tariffs by 2001, remove all oil price controls and end quantitative restrictions on imports by January 1, 1997. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The agreement includes the early privatisation and modernisation of Polish oil refineries, which will be obliged to offer equal treatment to all buyers. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The EU and Poland will monitor the settlement at six-monthly meetings. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Cyberspace squabbles overshadow copyright talks. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: GENEVA 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: In a gloomy Geneva conference centre built before the dawn of the Internet, groups of staid officials made a first stab on Friday at rewriting copyright laws for the digital age. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: But critics at the first government-level meeting to revise copyright laws in 25 years said the officials and legislators might as well be trying to police the ether. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: After four days of diplomatic wrangling over procedures, some 600 delegates from nations small and large got down to the nitty-gritty of setting the digital agenda for the first time. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Cyberspace squabbles overshadowed the debate on a stack of proposals covering literary and artistic works, the rights of performers and producers of music and producers of databases. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "If it goes on like this, we won't have enough time to finish all the discussions," a frustrated Western delegate said. " Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: They announced they will start evening sessions next week. " Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Attempts by copyright-based industries to ensure they get a cut from online works led to a storm of protests by Internet companies and critics who say the pacts would curb public access to online information from soccer results to stock prices. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "It's not illegal to make photocopies of newspaper articles. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: It's fair use. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: We can read sports statistics or stock prices. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: But with the treaty, this kind of fact will be owned and subject to licensing, "said James Love, a consumer lobbyist heading the Washington-based Consumer Project on Technology. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "None of the treaties are ready to move. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: These people don't understand what they're doing. " Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: At stake are billions of dollars and the future of the electronic information industry -- the coming medium for the distribution of music, films, literature, software and commerce. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Supporters of the three pacts say they are only an extension of existing intellectual property rights, covered by the century-old Berne Convention. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: But an array of opponents from the network industry to consumer, scientific and academic groups say the pacts will give sweeping powers to entertainment and copyright-based industries. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: A quick survey at the conference centre found few officials who had actually surfed the Internet. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Mongolia's state copyright official, Gundegma Jargalshaihan, said apologetically that he had just arrived from Ulan Bator and was not aware of the details of the digital agenda. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "We don't have money for Internet in Mongolia," he added. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Alexander Bavykin, deputy legal chief at Russia's foreign ministry, said Moscow had yet to formulate a policy on copyright in cybersppace. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: He too had never browsed the Net. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "I've never tried it and why should I? Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: There are lots of other things in this life I haven't tried either, "he said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: A visit to the computer centre offering Internet services found a lone European official clicking away on his mouse. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "Internet is a potential cash cow for copyright-based industries and we need roadmaps on the information superhighway," said Marc Pearl, vice-president of the Information Technology Association of America, a trade association of U.S. network companies opposing the treaties. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "But there are a lot of dinosaurs here. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: People here don't understand Internet technology. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Because they don't understand technology, they fear the unknown. " Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Before the Internet, those whose business was to protect copyrights knew where they stood. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Their enemies were tangible if elusive, such as the people who pirated music cassettes. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: But the Internet, a global computer network where anything from music to software can be duplicated and distributed at the click of a computer mouse, has ripped up the rulebooks. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Network operators said the draft laws would hold them responsible for copyright infringements in the system and expose them to multi-billion-dollar liabilities. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "There are 500 million messages transmitted through the Internet everyday," said Tim Casey of the U.S.-based MCI Communications Corporation. " Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: How can we control them all? " Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: FEATURE - Singapore sees prestige in hosting WTO. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Ramthan Hussain Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: SINGAPORE 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Singapore's winning campaign to host the World Trade Organisation (WTO)'s first ministerial meeting reflected its ambition to play a key role in shaping global free trade, the lifeblood of its economy, analysts said. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "As one of the world's most externally oriented economies, Singapore has a disproportionately large stake in the WTO," said Desmond Supple, economist at research house I.D.E.A. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "Singapore stands to benefit more than most from continued global trade liberalisation as trade is the engine of its growth, accounting for nearly three times its gross domestic product." Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The city-state met U.S. opposition two years ago in its bid to host the meeting, expected to gather 4,000 officials from 160 countries from December 9 to 13. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: In a stand some analysts linked to controversy over Singapore's caning of an American teenager for vandalism, then-U.S. Trade Representative Mickey Kantor had said the meeting ought to be held where the WTO was going to be headquartered. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: That would have meant Geneva. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: But Singapore had the support of other WTO members. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Derek da Cunha, senior fellow at the Institute of Policy Studies (ISEAS), said Singapore's hosting of the conference "carries a great deal of symbolism for the city-state, underscoring its commitment to free trade and its trading links across the globe." Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: There is the international prestige Singapore would enjoy, but "more importantly there is a genuine national interest in fostering better global free trade and an open market", said Tan Kong Yam, head of Business Policy at the National University of Singapore. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: At the ministerial meeting, trade ministers will review the work of the WTO and the implementation of the Uruguay Round free trade commitments under its predecessor the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT). Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: In June, the WTO hailed Singapore for its open market policies but the European Union and other trading powers called on Singapore to speed up the opening of its services sector. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Supple said the struggle that Singapore had to wage in vying to host the meeting would be repeated during the talks. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "There is tension at every step of the way," since a battle line between the West and developing countries has been drawn over the issue of linking trade liberalisation with labour rights, he said. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Supple said hosting the meeting carried prestige for Singapore, "however, this is quite intangible as the prestige factor may not necessarily lead to any additional investment and trade flows to this region." Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: From a commercial point of view, the meeting would be good for Singapore's tourism industry, Tan said. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: A large part of Singapore's workforce would be mobilised to ensure the meeting would run without a glitch but the average Singaporean "would probably not be too concerned about some of the issues," Tan said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "But the more educated public will realise that these kind of things are important for Singapore as a small economy." Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Supple said any political gains the Singapore government would get from the WTO meeting -- ahead of a general election due by April 1997 -- would depend on how successful it was in pushing its economic agenda. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "If there are any movements toward freer trade, then Singapore's economy and the electorate would gain," he said. " Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: But I don't think it would be wise to play up the political aspect of this. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: I think political issues will take secondary importance to all these economic issues that will be displayed. " Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Japan NTT says hopes to start int'l business soon. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: TOKYO 1996-12-06 Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) said on Friday that it hopes to move into the international telecommunications business as soon as possible following the government's decision to split NTT into three firms under a holding company. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "We hope to start international telephone business as soon as possible," a company official told Reuters. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The official said the latest government decision to split the company under a holding company would allow flexibility in NTT's international phone business. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Earlier, Posts and Telecommunications Minister Hisao Horinouchi told a news conference the government plans to split NTT into three firms under a holding company, but did not specify when the restructuring would likely take effect. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: One of the three new companies will be a long-distance operator and the other two will be local-call operators, Horinouchi said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: One of the local firms will operate in west Japan and the other in east Japan, he added. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The long-distance operator will offer international services, Horinouchi said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The NTT official said the timing of the planned split-up was uncertain because more discussions by government officials were required. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: CRICKET - WOOLMER MAKES SENTIMENTAL RETURN TO KANPUR. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: KANPUR, India 1996-12-07 Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: South Africa's trip to Kanpur for the third test against India has given former England test cricketer Bob Woolmer the chance of a sentimental return to his birthplace. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Woolmer was born in the northern city of Kanpur when his father worked there for an insurance compnay and was himself an active cricketer. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "It's been a sentimental journey ... Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: A visit to India is always an intriguing experience, "Woolmer, now the South African coach, said on Saturday. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Woolmer, 48, played 19 tests for England between 1975 and 1981. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: His first cricketing sojurn to India was as a member of Tony Greig's England side in 1976-77. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: His father Clarence Woolmer represented United Province, now renamed Uttar Pradesh, in India's Ranji Trophy national championship and captained the state during 1949. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Now aged 86, Woolmer senior lives with his son in Cape Town. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Woolmer's memories of Kanpur are few and blurred. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "I don't remember much of the place," he said. " Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: I came here on zero and left at three (aged three) when my father was transferred to Calcutta where I spent another four and half years. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "But I do remember we had a cobra snake in the basement of our house. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Also that my father bought a bicycle and when we rode over a hose pipe it broke into two. " Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Woolmer said the hospital where he was born is close to the stadium where the India-South Africa test will be played. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: CRICKET - JONES HITS CENTURY AS VICTORIA FIGHT BACK. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: HOBART, Australia 1996-12-07 Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Former Australia test batsman Dean Jones hit an unbeaten 130 to lead Victoria's fightback in their Sheffield Shield match against Tasmania on Saturday. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Replying to the home side's first innings 481 for eight declared, Victoria reached 220 for three at close of play on the second day of the four-day match at Hobart's Bellerive Oval. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Jones became the fourth century-maker of the match, equalling the feats of Tasmanian trio David Boon, Shaun Young and Michael DiVenuto. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Jones, who took over as captain for the match in the absence of Australia test leg-spinner Shane Warne, added 195 runs for the third wicket with left-hander Laurie Harper. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Harper was eventually dismissed for 77 after the pair joined forces with their side reeling on nine for two. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Earlier, former Australia test batsman David Boon scored 118 and all-rounder Shaun Young hit 113. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The pair hammered 36 boundaries between them. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Pace bowler Ian Harvey claimed three for 81 for Victoria. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: SOCCER - SOUTH KOREA MOVE CLOSE TO QUARTER-FINAL BERTH. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: ABU DHABI 1996-12-07 Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: South Korea made virtually certain of an Asian Cup quarter-final spot with a 4-2 win over Indonesia in a Group A match on Saturday. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: After going four up in the first 55 minutes South Korea allowed Indonesia, newcomers to Asian Cup finals, back into the match, conceding two goals from rare counter attacks. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Kim Do Hoon opened the scoring for South Korea in only the fifth minute, turning unmarked on the penalty spot to fire a shot into the top corner. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: It looked like turning into a rout as Hwang Sun Hong rapidly added two more in the seventh and 15th minutes but although the Koreans continued to dominate they failed to add to the score before the interval. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: But they started the second half where they had left off and it was not long before they went four up, Ko Jeong Woon heading in from a free kick in the 55th minute. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: The Koreans then appeared to relax, allowing the Indonesians to get back into the match. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Ronny Wabia scored for Indonesia three minutes later direct from a a corner kick that Korean goalkeeper Kim Byung reached with one hand but failed to keep out. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: With 65 minutes gone Indonesia's Widodo Putra, who scored a spectacular goal against Kuwait on Wednesday, was again on target, breaking through the Korean defence to beat the keeper with a low shot. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Indonesian keeper Hendro Kartiko produced a string of fine saves to prevent the Koreans increasing their lead. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Vancouver Canucks star right wing Pavel Bure was suspended for one game by the National Hockey League and fined $1,000 Friday for his hit on Buffalo Sabres defenceman Garry Galley on Wednesday. Following the order: first to last Entity:

input_text: Sentence: Bure received a double-minor penalty for high-sticking with 2:22 left in the first period of Wednesday's 7-6 overtime win by Vancouver after colliding with Galley in Buffalo zone. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Galley suffered a concussion and did not return to the game. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "Mr Bure left his feet to deliver a forearm blow to Mr Galley as he was about to be checked legally by his opponent," said NHL discipline chief Brian Burke in handing out the suspension. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: "Although it is clear from the videotape that Mr Bure's actions were a reaction to the impending hit and there was no intent to injure his opponent, there can be no excuse for this type of conduct," Burke said. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: SOCCER - ENGLISHMAN CHARLTON IS MADE AN HONORARY IRISHMAN. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: DUBLIN 1996-12-07 Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Jack Charlton's relationship with the people of Ireland was cemented on Saturday when the Englishman was officially declared one of their own. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: Charlton, 61, and his wife, Peggy, became citizens of Ireland when they formally received Irish passports from deputy Prime Minister Dick Spring who said the honour had been made in recognition of Charlton's achievements as the national soccer manager. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "The years I spent as manager of the Republic of Ireland were the best years of my life. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: It all culminated in the fact that I now have lots of great, great friends in Ireland. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: That is why this is so emotional a night for me, "Charlton said. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: "It was the joy that we all had over the period, that I shared with people that I grew to love, that I treasure most," he added. Following the order: first to last Entity:
Sentence: Charlton managed Ireland for 93 matches, during which time they lost only 17 times in almost 10 years until he resigned in December 1995. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: He guided Ireland to two successive World Cup finals tournaments and to the 1988 European championship finals in Germany, after the Irish beat a well-fancied England team 1-0 in their group qualifier. Following the order: first to last Entity:

Sentence: The lanky former Leeds United defender did not make his England debut until the age of 30 but eventually won 35 caps and was a key member of the 1966 World Cup winning team with his younger brother, Bobby. Following the order: first to last Entity:
